sections.name: The Fastest Surgeon in History
lines: Before anaesthetic, surgery was a race against pain. And Robert Liston was the fastest surgeon alive.
Patients were awake for everything. The only painkillers were alcohol, and strong assistants.
So Liston worked fast. He could take off a leg in about two and a half minutes.
He'd shout at the students. Time me, gentlemen. Time me.
In 1846, he became one of the first surgeons in Britain to operate with ether, with the patient fast asleep.
Afterwards he told the crowd, this Yankee dodge beats mesmerism hollow.
